unit.why: A short anecdote, told by the Karliner rebbe, about R. Aharon of Karlin quietly reciting the Song of Songs after the Friday-night meal and the Maggid asking him to stop. It is set inside a kabbalistic remark on raising and lowering waters.

stories.start_quote: הה״ק מקארלין דיבר מענין התקשרות ואהבת צדיקים
stories.summary_en: The Karliner rebbe tells that his grandfather R. Aharon recited the Song of Songs inaudibly in his lodging after the Sabbath-eve meal, yet the Maggid of Mezeritch sent word asking him to stop because he could not sleep while it was being said; the grandfather also set out twelve hallot at his master's table.

tags.why: The story is about the bond between R. Aharon and his master, the Maggid.
It is set on Friday night and at the Sabbath meals.

quotes: ואמר שיה״ש בחשאי שלא נשמע לשום ב"א
שלא היה יכול לישן כ"ז שאומר שיה״ש
tags.why: The Maggid perceives a recitation that no human could hear.
The anecdote is framed by the kabbalistic concepts of mayin nukvin and mayin dukhrin.

quotes: דיבר מענין התקשרות ואהבת צדיקים זה לזה
tags.why: The narrative is wrapped in a doctrinal remark about love between tsaddikim.
A named tsaddik narrates the tale about his grandfather.

quotes: אא"ז ז"ל היה בבחינת העלאת מ"נ
tags.why: The protagonist is the narrating tsaddik's grandfather.
The theme is the attachment between tsaddikim.

quotes: ושלח רבו הק׳ לבקש מאתו שיפסיק
tags.why: The two figures interact through a messenger.
